purpose: Lower-confidence pricing signals - verbal ballparks, budgetary estimates, informal contractor conversations. This is explicitly NOT the same tier as tests/../mike_quote_records_pearland_202605.json, which holds only verified, formal, written proposals with model numbers and full scope. Market evidence informs pattern-spotting over time; it should never be presented to a customer as a market benchmark on its own, and should never be averaged with or substituted for verified quote data.

knowledgeLayers.layer1_generalKnowledge: What the underlying model already knows about HVAC in general - no metro-specific grounding, this is the default/fallback.
knowledgeLayers.layer2_marketEvidence: This file. Every quote/pricing conversation collected, tagged by city, date, brand, equipment, scope, and confidence - useful for spotting patterns as volume grows, not yet reliable enough to state as fact.
knowledgeLayers.layer3_verifiedQuotes: Only detailed written proposals with model numbers and full scope - see the Pearland quote records file. This is the gold-standard tier Mike should eventually learn from most heavily.

rules: Never treat a single market evidence entry as sufficient to state a price range as fact to a customer.

A pattern only starts to mean something once multiple independent entries (ideally from different sources) converge on a similar range for genuinely comparable equipment/scope - one data point is a data point, not a benchmark.

Always keep 'ballpark estimate' / 'budgetary estimate' / 'formal written proposal' distinct - see BUYING READINESS section of the system prompt for the customer-facing version of this same distinction.
Redact any personal information before an entry goes in this file - these are meant to be shareable/referenceable without privacy concern.

entries.estimateTypeNote: Verbal ballpark from a Home Depot representative, not a formal written proposal - lowest-reliability tier of evidence.

systemDetails.note: Not specified in the verbal estimate - typical of ballpark-tier evidence; formal proposals will generally have this level of detail, ballparks generally won't.

entries.notes: First live market signal collected. Useful as a single reference point for the Columbus metro, but not enough on its own to state 'a full Rheem system in Columbus costs $14k-16k' as fact - see rules above. Would need several more independent entries, ideally including at least one formal written proposal, before this range could be treated as reasonably reliable.
